scenes.tts: Label the new proteins a pancreas cell makes in a few minutes. An hour later, where are they? Could the proteins themselves tell you how far they have come?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9, filling about 70% of frame height). One secretory cell drawn as a left-to-right line of stations inside a rounded BLUE cell outline: at the far left the rough ER (three stacked BLUE flat sacs dotted with small GREY ribosome dots); then the ERGIC (three small BLUE circles); then three tall BLUE Golgi cisternae side by side; then the TGN (a BLUE tubular net). Right of the TGN the line forks: the upper branch runs to a gap in the thick BLUE plasma membrane on the right edge (the door); the lower branch runs to a row of empty round granule outlines just inside the membrane (the shelf). A thin GREY flow arrow runs under the whole line, pointing right, and its chevrons drift slowly rightward all film long. Top-left: a chase clock reading 'min 0'. Bottom-right corner: an empty gel panel with four lanes headed 0, 15, 30, 60 and two band positions labelled 'uncut' (higher) and 'cut' (lower). Colours by concept for the whole film: GOLD = the labelled cargo cohort; GREY = unlabelled protein; TEAL = the ER chaperone and its KDEL tail; WHITE = the KDEL receptor; dashed RED = the mannosidase II line; SAND (#D9C3A0) = constitutive carriers; dark granule membranes with GOLD packed inside = regulated granules. Sugar trees use cartoon symbols only (GREEN circles mannose, BLUE circles glucose, BLUE squares GlcNAc, YELLOW circles galactose, PURPLE diamonds sialic acid), always labelled 'schematic'. Opening action: the ribosome dots on the ER flash and emit small GOLD dots into the ER lumen for 3 s while a white tag 'pulse' blinks beside the clock. On 'An hour later' the clock spins from 0 to 60 and the GOLD dots blur into a smear along the line, with a large white '?' over the stations. On 'the proteins themselves' a round zoom bubble opens over one GOLD dot showing a tiny sugar tree with a white '?' on it. The question appears across the top in white: 'Where are they? Can they tell you?'
scenes.narration: Label the new proteins a pancreas cell makes in a few minutes. An hour later, where are they? Could the proteins themselves tell you how far they have come?

scenes.visual: Title 'Forward Is the Default' fades in over the top of the world for 2 s and the hook question fades out under it. The flow-arrow chevrons keep drifting right; the clock resets to 'min 0'.

scenes.tts: A pulse-chase gives a brief pulse of radioactive amino acid, then a flood of the unlabelled one. Only the batch made during the pulse is labelled: the cohort.
scenes.visual: On 'pulse' the ribosomes emit GOLD dots for a moment (tag 'pulse'); on 'flood' they switch to emitting GREY dots (tag 'chase'), which keep trickling in behind for the rest of the film. On 'the cohort' the GOLD dots, gathered in the ER, get the label 'cohort'.
scenes.narration: A pulse-chase gives a brief pulse of radioactive amino acid, then a flood of the unlabelled one. Only the batch made during the pulse is labelled: the cohort.

scenes.tts: Caro and Palade did this in the guinea-pig pancreas. Silver grains in a photographic layer marked the label. At about five minutes they lay over the rough E R. At about twenty, over the Golgi. At about an hour, over the storage granules.
scenes.caption: Caro and Palade did this in the guinea-pig pancreas. Silver grains in a photographic layer marked the label. At about 5 minutes they lay over the rough ER. At about 20, over the Golgi. At about an hour, over the storage granules.
scenes.visual: Small caption 'Lucien Caro & George Palade, 1964' under the clock. On 'silver grains' a thin translucent layer slides over the cell (label 'photographic layer') and small WHITE grain dots sprinkle where the GOLD cohort is. The clock runs: on 'five minutes' it reads 5 and most grains sit over the ER; on 'twenty' it reads 20 and the densest grains sit over the Golgi; on 'an hour' it reads 60 and they sit over the granule outlines, which fill GOLD. The cohort is drawn as a spread cloud with a bright peak, never a compact cluster. Grey dots fill the stations behind. Corner label: 'grain positions: schematic'.
scenes.narration: Caro and Palade did this in the guinea-pig pancreas. Silver grains in a photographic layer marked the label. At about 5 minutes they lay over the rough ER. At about 20, over the Golgi. At about an hour, over the storage granules.

scenes.tts: So the cohort's peak moves forward through a fixed order of stations, though it spreads out. The E R, a sorting dock, the Golgi stack, and the trans-Golgi network, where routes split.
scenes.caption: So the cohort's peak moves forward through a fixed order of stations, though it spreads out. The ER, a sorting dock, the Golgi stack, and the trans-Golgi network, where routes split.
scenes.visual: The clock resets to 0 and the GOLD cohort replays its trip as a broad glowing cloud whose brightest part moves left to right, with a faint tail left behind in earlier stations. As the peak reaches each station, that station brightens and its label rises beneath it and stays: 'rough ER', 'ERGIC: sorting dock', 'cis', 'medial', 'trans', 'TGN: routes split'. On 'spreads out' the cloud visibly widens. On 'routes split' the fork right of the TGN pulses: the upper branch toward the door and the lower branch toward the shelf.
scenes.narration: So the cohort's peak moves forward through a fixed order of stations, though it spreads out. The ER, a sorting dock, the Golgi stack, and the trans-Golgi network, where routes split.

scenes.tts: Now follow one protein. In the E R it gets a ready-made tree of fourteen sugars, trimmed as it folds. In the Golgi, enzymes in successive sacs cut and rebuild it, roughly in order. One, mannosidase two, marks a red line.
scenes.caption: Now follow one protein. In the ER it gets a ready-made tree of 14 sugars, trimmed as it folds. In the Golgi, enzymes in successive sacs cut and rebuild it, roughly in order. One, mannosidase II, marks a red line.
scenes.visual: Camera eases in so the ER-to-trans stretch fills the frame; one GOLD protein (a rounded blob) is followed. In the ER a schematic sugar tree drops onto it whole: 2 BLUE squares at the base, 9 GREEN circles branching above, 3 BLUE circles at the tips (label '14-sugar core, schematic'). The blob tightens from loose to compact (label 'folding') while the 3 BLUE tip circles pop off one by one. The protein drifts into the Golgi. Three soft, overlapping colour washes sit across the cisternae (enzyme zones); in the first, GREEN circles snip off and BLUE squares are added. On 'mannosidase two' a dashed RED vertical line draws down through the medial cisterna, label 'mannosidase II'; as the protein crosses it, two more GREEN circles snip off. Later, YELLOW circles (label 'galactose') and then PURPLE diamonds (label 'sialic acid') attach at the tips in the trans cisterna.
scenes.narration: Now follow one protein. In the ER it gets a ready-made tree of 14 sugars, trimmed as it folds. In the Golgi, enzymes in successive sacs cut and rebuild it, roughly in order. One, mannosidase II, marks a red line.

scenes.tts: But these enzymes overlap from sac to sac, so the tree cannot say which sac the protein is in. It records the enzymes it has met: a rough odometer, not an address.
scenes.visual: The overlapping enzyme washes pulse to show they spill across neighbouring cisternae. A label 'which sac?' appears over the protein, wobbles and fades. Beside the tree a short row of small stamps appears, one per processing step the tree has been through ('glucoses off', 'mannoses off', 'GlcNAc on', 'mannosidase II', 'galactose', 'sialic acid'); a stamp lights as each change replays, and two stamps on a side branch stay unlit to show the record branches. Label under the row: 'enzymes met, not an address'. No rolling digits and no reverse arrow.
scenes.narration: But these enzymes overlap from sac to sac, so the tree cannot say which sac the protein is in. It records the enzymes it has met: a rough odometer, not an address.

scenes.tts: To read the record, sample at each chase time and treat each sample with an enzyme, Endo H. It cuts chains still mostly mannose, but not those rebuilt past mannosidase two. Cut protein loses sugar and runs faster on a gel. Over the chase, the cut band gives way to the uncut one.
scenes.visual: Zoom back out to the whole world. The clock runs 0, 15, 30, 60; at each time a pipette draws a small aliquot of the cell's GOLD protein into one of four sample tubes OUTSIDE the cell (labels 0, 15, 30, 60). A TEAL-outlined scissors icon labelled 'Endo H' acts only in the tubes: it snips trees that are still mostly GREEN mannose circles and leaves uncut any tree whose mannose branch has been trimmed away, with or without YELLOW and PURPLE tips; the decision follows the tree's shape, not any position in the cell. Each tube empties into one gel lane: the 'uncut' band at 0, 33, 55 and 80% intensity and the 'cut' band (lower, label 'cut: lost sugar, runs faster') at 100, 67, 45 and 20% (the lesson's illustrative worked problem; label 'illustrative data'). On 'gives way' the brightness shifts visibly across the four lanes.
scenes.caption: To read the record, sample at each chase time and treat each sample with an enzyme, Endo H. It cuts chains still mostly mannose, but not those rebuilt past mannosidase II. Cut protein loses sugar and runs faster on a gel. Over the chase, the cut band gives way to the uncut one.
scenes.narration: To read the record, sample at each chase time and treat each sample with an enzyme, Endo H. It cuts chains still mostly mannose, but not those rebuilt past mannosidase II. Cut protein loses sugar and runs faster on a gel. Over the chase, the cut band gives way to the uncut one.

scenes.tts: Some proteins should stay. E R chaperones, which help others fold, leak forward too. Many end in a tag, K D E L. Past the E R, in slightly acidic compartments, a receptor grabs the tag. A coated vesicle carries both back, and in the near-neutral E R the receptor lets go.
scenes.caption: Some proteins should stay. ER chaperones, which help others fold, leak forward too. Many end in a tag, KDEL. Past the ER, in slightly acidic compartments, a receptor grabs the tag. A coated vesicle carries both back, and in the near-neutral ER the receptor lets go.
scenes.visual: A TEAL rounded chaperone with a short TEAL tail labelled 'KDEL' drifts out of the ER among the GOLD cargo and into the ERGIC. A small tag 'slightly acidic' appears over the ERGIC and cis cisterna. A WHITE receptor block in the ERGIC membrane, labelled 'KDEL receptor', closes on the tail. A BLUE vesicle with a spiky coat outline (label 'COPI vesicle') buds off carrying both and travels LEFT, against the drifting flow chevrons, along a TEAL return arrow. At the ER a tag 'near neutral' appears; the receptor opens and the chaperone floats free in the ER lumen. The TEAL return loop stays drawn faintly for the rest of the film.
scenes.narration: Some proteins should stay. ER chaperones, which help others fold, leak forward too. Many end in a tag, KDEL. Past the ER, in slightly acidic compartments, a receptor grabs the tag. A coated vesicle carries both back, and in the near-neutral ER the receptor lets go.

scenes.tts: Now snip the tag off. Sean Munro and Hugh Pelham did this to the chaperone G R P seventy-eight, in cultured monkey cells. Where does it end up?
scenes.caption: Now snip the tag off. Sean Munro and Hugh Pelham did this to the chaperone grp78, in cultured monkey cells. Where does it end up?
scenes.visual: Zoom on a second TEAL chaperone in the ER, label 'grp78'. A small pair of WHITE scissors cut off its 'KDEL' tail, which fades away; the new label reads 'grp78, KDEL deleted'. Small caption 'Munro & Pelham, 1987, COS cells'. Question card in white across the top: 'Where does it end up?'
scenes.narration: Now snip the tag off. Sean Munro and Hugh Pelham did this to the chaperone grp78, in cultured monkey cells. Where does it end up?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the tagless TEAL chaperone bobs slowly in the ER, the flow chevrons keep drifting right, and the WHITE receptors in the ERGIC wait with open jaws.

scenes.tts: It is secreted with the cargo, because its KDEL tag is gone. For soluble cargo in animal cells, forward is the default unless a protein is held, fetched back, or sorted out.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. The tagless TEAL chaperone rides right with a GOLD group, passes the open WHITE receptors (they do not close), crosses the Golgi and the TGN, takes the upper branch and leaves through the door; outside, a label 'secreted'. On 'Forward is the default' large white text appears across the top and stays to the end of the scene: 'Forward is the default'. On 'holds it' a GOLD tangled blob in the ER gets a tag 'held: not folded'; on 'fetches it back' the faint TEAL return loop brightens; on 'sorts it out' the shelf of granules glows.
scenes.narration: It is secreted with the cargo, because its KDEL tag is gone. For soluble cargo in animal cells, forward is the default unless a protein is held, fetched back, or sorted out.

scenes.tts: For soluble cargo, the trans-Golgi network can split the routes. Some carriers go straight to the surface: constitutive secretion, the default door. In this cell, digestive enzymes are sorted into granules instead: regulated secretion. They wait on a shelf until a stimulus releases them. Does that stimulus also speed up the line?
scenes.visual: Camera eases right so the TGN, the fork, the door and the shelf fill the frame. SAND carriers bud from the TGN and fuse with the membrane at the door in a steady stream, label 'constitutive: the door'. GOLD cargo packs densely into dark-membrane granules that line up on the shelf, label 'regulated: the shelf'. On 'a stimulus' a WHITE pulse ring labelled 'stimulus' sweeps in from outside; the granules fuse with the membrane and empty their GOLD outside. On 'speed up the line' a white '?' appears over the ER-to-Golgi stretch and stays, unanswered, to the end of the scene.
scenes.narration: For soluble cargo, the trans-Golgi network can split the routes. Some carriers go straight to the surface: constitutive secretion, the default door. In this cell, digestive enzymes are sorted into granules instead: regulated secretion. They wait on a shelf until a stimulus releases them. Does that stimulus also speed up the line?

scenes.tts: So where are the labelled proteins an hour later? Mostly in storage granules. A glycoprotein among them can carry a sugar record of the enzymes it met. For soluble cargo, going on is the default. Staying means being held or fetched back. Storing means being sorted, in ways still argued.
scenes.visual: Zoom back out to the whole world; the clock jumps to 60. The hook's question returns faintly at the top. The GOLD cohort is shown mostly in the granules on the shelf, with a faint tail behind, grey protein behind it. The row of processing stamps reappears beside one granule, mostly lit. On 'Going on is the default' the flow chevrons brighten; on 'held or fetched back' the tangled blob in the ER and the TEAL loop glow; on 'sorted' the shelf glows. The question fades as the answer finishes.
scenes.narration: So where are the labelled proteins an hour later? Mostly in storage granules. A glycoprotein among them can carry a sugar record of the enzymes it met. For soluble cargo, going on is the default. Staying means being held or fetched back. Storing means being sorted, in ways still argued.

scenes.line: Forward is the default for soluble cargo, unless held, retrieved or sorted.
scenes.visual: End card: 'Forward is the default for soluble cargo, unless held, retrieved or sorted.' over the softly drifting world.
